newsitem.title: JAPAN: Volvo, Mitsubishi Motors to step up cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Volvo, Mitsubishi Motors to step up cooperation.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp and Sweden's Volvo have agreed to strengthen their business ties and will explore ways of cooperating in sales and car components, the Japanese car maker said on Tuesday.
Mitsubishi, Japan's fourth biggest auto maker, said the aim of the closer collaboration was to boost competitiveness.
Under an existing tie-up, Volvo and Mitsubishi produce cars at their Dutch joint venture NedCar, which is owned in three equal parts by the car firms and the Dutch government.
"We have agreed to strengthen our tie-up," a Mitsubishi Motors spokesman said.
The spokesman said the two companies will consider jointly selling commercial vehicles in Europe. They will also consider sharing car components globally and developing a new engine, he said.
"They are broad directions and details will need to be discussed," the Mitsubishi spokesman said.
"The agreement was made in order to increase competitiveness," he added.
